The George Washington University

Steps away from World-class Opportunities

 

 

At the George Washington University, countless new possibilities, new opportunities, and new discoveries

are closer than ever.

Find Your Program

Visit

Apply

 

 

 

Image
Image

GW Revolutionaries have a story to tell. Read their stories of how they’ve stepped forward into new possibilities to drive progress and push the boundaries of what’s possible on a campus without borders, in a city where world-class opportunities are just steps away.

↔ Swipe left/right

Image

Camila Barbosa

Sophomore • International Affairs • Elliott School of International Affairs

Whether it’s gaining experience on the international, national or local level, Camila’s GW education puts her just steps away from her goals. The international relations and criminal justice double major has been an intern on Capitol Hill in Representative Darren Soto’s (JD ’04) office and the Embassy of El Salvador where she helped develop trade policy reports. This fall, she will intern for the DC Metro Police Department. Plus, Camila has learned firsthand from judges and attorneys as a member of GW’s Mock Trial team.

 

Image

Sylvain Guiriec

Associate Professor • Physics • Columbian College of Arts and Sciences

Dr. Sylvain Guiriec proves that GW is a launch pad in more ways than one. Dr. Guiriec and his GW students work on cutting-edge projects in partnership with NASA, from developing X-ray space telescopes and launching satellites to mapping gamma-ray bursts. The GW physics professor and astrophysicist at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center leads GW’s partnership with NASA, creating student and faculty research opportunities at Goddard.

Image

Edlyn Rochon

M.P.H. ’26 and Ph.D. Candidate • Public Health • Milken Institute School of Public Health

Edlyn hopes her passion for knowledge and her community will have a big impact. Working full-time at GW's Gill-Lebovic Center, Edlyn applies systems thinking frameworks to examine the complex, interconnected social determinants of health within Latino populations, driving equity through structural and policy-level solutions. This work holds a special connection for Edlyn, whose parents came to the D.C. area from their native El Salvador. The first-generation college graduate is now back at GW’s Milken Institute School of Public Health (SPH) to pursue her Ph.D.

Image

Amir Arrington

Senior • Business • GW School of Business

In the nation’s capital “where everybody’s on the move,” the senior business major, men’s basketball walk-on, Posse scholar and budding entrepreneur is keeping pace and thriving in his element. Priding himself on the relationship-building lessons he’s gained from GWSB, Amir has amassed an international network of students, alumni and local executives who have provided hands-on learning opportunities in real estate, hospitality and entrepreneurship. In turn, Amir is applying these real-life lessons to his own start-up, the AthLead Network.

 

 

 

Make an Impact

Image

GW Research is Transforming Lives

Every day, researchers at the George Washington University take on some of the world’s toughest challenges, delivering real-world impact and insights through their relentless pursuit of knowledge and a deeper understanding of our world. From advancing cancer therapies and the prevention of diabetes in at-risk populations, to building trustworthy AI systems and next-generation computer chips, much of their work is made possible through vital federal investments.

With support from the National Institutes of Health, the National Science Foundation, NASA, the Department of Defense and other federal agencies, GW advances medical innovations, fuels economic growth, and prepares the next generation of leaders.

Discover the Impact of Federally-Funded Research at GW

The former Polish president shared his views on current global challenges and the need to strengthen a commitment to global democracy.

A Diverse Community is a Strong Community

Collaboration, Respect, Openness and Diversity are core values that define the George Washington University (GW). The Accessibility Notice and Equal Opportunity (EO) Statement shared here reflect our desire to make this a welcoming and inclusive space for all students, visitors and members of our broader community.

 

 

Accessibility Notice

The George Washington University (GW) is committed to making all web properties and web content accessible and usable for everyone, including people with disabilities, by employing principles of universal design and striving to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.

If you experience a barrier that affects your ability to access GW websites, videos or other digital content, please let us know.

 

Equal Opportunity (EO) Statement

The George Washington University does not unlawfully discriminate against any person on any basis prohibited by federal law, the District of Columbia Human Rights Act, or other applicable law, including without limitation, age, color, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry and ethnic characteristics), pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, and/or other characteristics protected by applicable law. This policy covers all programs, services, policies, and procedures of the university, including admission to education programs and employment.

The George Washington University does not unlawfully discriminate against any person on any basis prohibited by federal law, the District of Columbia Human Rights Act, or other applicable law, including without limitation, age, color, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry and ethnic characteristics), pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, and/or other characteristics protected by applicable law. This policy covers all programs, services, policies, and procedures of the university, including admission to education programs and employment.

The George Washington University

Steps away from World-class Opportunities

 

 

At the George Washington University, countless new possibilities, new opportunities, and new discoveries

are closer than ever.

Find Your Program

Visit

Apply

 

 

 

Image
Image

GW Revolutionaries have a story to tell. Read their stories of how they’ve stepped forward into new possibilities to drive progress and push the boundaries of what’s possible on a campus without borders, in a city where world-class opportunities are just steps away.

↔ Swipe left/right

Image

Camila Barbosa

Sophomore • International Affairs • Elliott School of International Affairs

Whether it’s gaining experience on the international, national or local level, Camila’s GW education puts her just steps away from her goals. The international relations and criminal justice double major has been an intern on Capitol Hill in Representative Darren Soto’s (JD ’04) office and the Embassy of El Salvador where she helped develop trade policy reports. This fall, she will intern for the DC Metro Police Department. Plus, Camila has learned firsthand from judges and attorneys as a member of GW’s Mock Trial team.

 

Image

Sylvain Guiriec

Associate Professor • Physics • Columbian College of Arts and Sciences

Dr. Sylvain Guiriec proves that GW is a launch pad in more ways than one. Dr. Guiriec and his GW students work on cutting-edge projects in partnership with NASA, from developing X-ray space telescopes and launching satellites to mapping gamma-ray bursts. The GW physics professor and astrophysicist at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center leads GW’s partnership with NASA, creating student and faculty research opportunities at Goddard.

Image

Edlyn Rochon

M.P.H. ’26 and Ph.D. Candidate • Public Health • Milken Institute School of Public Health

Edlyn hopes her passion for knowledge and her community will have a big impact. Working full-time at GW's Gill-Lebovic Center, Edlyn applies systems thinking frameworks to examine the complex, interconnected social determinants of health within Latino populations, driving equity through structural and policy-level solutions. This work holds a special connection for Edlyn, whose parents came to the D.C. area from their native El Salvador. The first-generation college graduate is now back at GW’s Milken Institute School of Public Health (SPH) to pursue her Ph.D.

Image

Amir Arrington

Senior • Business • GW School of Business

In the nation’s capital “where everybody’s on the move,” the senior business major, men’s basketball walk-on, Posse scholar and budding entrepreneur is keeping pace and thriving in his element. Priding himself on the relationship-building lessons he’s gained from GWSB, Amir has amassed an international network of students, alumni and local executives who have provided hands-on learning opportunities in real estate, hospitality and entrepreneurship. In turn, Amir is applying these real-life lessons to his own start-up, the AthLead Network.

 

 

 

Make an Impact

Image

GW Research is Transforming Lives

Every day, researchers at the George Washington University take on some of the world’s toughest challenges, delivering real-world impact and insights through their relentless pursuit of knowledge and a deeper understanding of our world. From advancing cancer therapies and the prevention of diabetes in at-risk populations, to building trustworthy AI systems and next-generation computer chips, much of their work is made possible through vital federal investments.

With support from the National Institutes of Health, the National Science Foundation, NASA, the Department of Defense and other federal agencies, GW advances medical innovations, fuels economic growth, and prepares the next generation of leaders.

Discover the Impact of Federally-Funded Research at GW
